warnings: THIS SHEET ANSWERS THE PILE-COUNT QUESTION S-01 LEFT OPEN. S-01's footing plan draws each footing as an outline with a single square at its centre and prints no pile count, so that file records none rather than guessing. The enlargements here state it outright: F1 = เสาเข็ม 1 ต้น (450x450 cap), F2 = เสาเข็ม 2 ต้น (1050x450 cap). With S-01's counts that is 12 x 1 + 4 x 2 = 20 piles for the house.

THE COLUMN SCHEDULE IS A MULTI-LEVEL TABLE AND IS RECORDED PER §8: the same mark repeats once per level with a separate level field, never merged and never with the level baked into element_id. C1 and C2 each get three rows (ชั้นบน / ชั้นล่าง / ตอม่อ), six entries in all. §4's point-element merge rule deliberately does NOT apply here - that rule is for elements with a position on a plan, and these rows have none.

C1's ชั้นล่าง CELL IS A DITTO ARROW, NOT A VALUE. The table draws an upward arrow in that cell meaning 'as ชั้นบน'. The row is recorded with the ชั้นบน values copied down and flagged cell_is_a_ditto_arrow_pointing_at_the_row_above, so nobody later mistakes it for an independent reading. C2 by contrast really does step up at ชั้นล่าง (0.15 -> 0.20, ø12 -> ø16), which is why the arrow appears on C1 only.

THE ELEMENT TYPE SPLITS BY LEVEL, ON PURPOSE. The two ชั้นบน/ชั้นล่าง rows are element_type column; the ตอม่อ row is element_type pedestal, matching how S-01 and S-01/1 label the same member on their plans (เสาตอม่อ). Same mark, two types, distinguished by level.

A UNIT TYPO ON THE SHEET, RECORDED AS PRINTED. C1's ชั้นบน cell prints 0.15x0.15 มม. - millimetres - where every sibling cell prints ม. A 0.15 mm column is physically impossible and C2's identical cell prints ม., so it is a typo on the drawing. width_mm/height_mm record 150 (i.e. 0.15 m) and the printed text is kept verbatim in printed_as with a flag. Nothing was silently corrected.

DB AND RB ARE PRINTED AS WORDS ON THIS SHEET, not as the Ø symbol used on S-04, so type follows the printed word directly: main bars DB (deformed), stirrups and slab mesh RB (round). This agrees with S-01's material note (ø6/ø9 = SR-24 round, ø12 and up = SD-30 deformed) - the only place in the set where the two conventions can be cross-checked, and they do agree.

TWO CAGES MIX DIAMETERS IN ONE MEMBER. F2 carries 8-DB 12 plus 5-DB 16 and C2's ตอม่อ carries 4-DB 16 plus 4-DB 12. Both are recorded as a single main_bar object per §0.6 with count = the total, mixed_dia_mm listing both, and the full printed text in count_printed_as. C2's ตอม่อ also prints 2ป (a double stirrup), kept in the stirrup note.

COLUMNS USE A SINGLE main_bar.count AND NEVER top/bottom, per §6. All six column/pedestal rows print one figure (4-DB 12, 4-DB 16, 4-DB 16 + 4DB 12) and are recorded that way; splitting them into top/bottom would silently double the real bar count.

FIVE SLAB MARKS ARE DETAILED - S, S1, S2, S3, GS - AND NO SG. That is the evidence used to resolve the SG/GS ambiguity on S-01's ground-floor plan; see that file's own warning. S1 and S2 appear on the upper floor (S-02), S3 is the cantilever slab, S and GS appear on both floors.

F1 and F2 here are PILE CAPS on S-01's pile foundation. The unindexed sheet S-01/1 uses the same letter F for three SPREAD footings (F1 / F1.5 / F1.8) with completely different sizes and reinforcement, detailed on that sheet. F1 therefore means two different members depending on which foundation option is built - element_type distinguishes them (pile_cap here, footing there) and each stays in its own file.
